newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude up on Iraq, Iran news, technicals.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude up on Iraq, Iran news, technicals.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil continued to make ground boosted by news of Iraq's plan to fly through a no-fly zone, further protests by Iranian students, cold weather forecasts in the U.S. and technical factors, brokers said.
June Brent crude oil had gained some 48 cents by 1505 GMT to trade at $18.40 a barrel.
The contract was attempting to fill a gap between $18.40 and $18.50 and had moved up to, but failed to hold, an intra-day high of $18.48.
'It's technical, Iran versus the U.S. and the Iraqi story as well as cold U.S. weather,' one broker said.
More than 1,000 Iranian students marched to the German embassy in Tehran on Monday to protest against a Berlin court verdict accusing Iran's leaders of ordering political killings, witnesses said.

Also on Monday Iraq said it was sending helicopters to pick up returning Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border despite a ban by the United States and other Western powers on Iraqi flights in the area.
The Iraqi News Agency said the decision was announced after a meeting in which Iraqi leaders headed by President Saddam Hussein warned the U.S. not to intercept the helicopters.
"Any American action threatening the safety of the helicopters and the pilgrims will be met with an appropriate action," the state news agency said, quoting an official source, without elaborating.
'It's like the Iraqi's are throwing down the gauntlet to the U.S. and they will have to react. That's how the market seems to be reading it anyway,' another broker said.
May gas oil gained some $2 to trade last at $165.25 boosted by gains on crude and NYMEX heating oil.
